name: Tadalafil

what.text: Tadalafil is a small-molecule drug called a PDE5 inhibitor. It is the active ingredient in Cialis, approved for erectile dysfunction (ED) and for symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH, an enlarged prostate that is not cancer), and in Adcirca, approved for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH).
How it acts, according to the FDA label

items.text: During sexual stimulation, nitric oxide from nerves and blood-vessel cells raises cGMP in penile smooth muscle. cGMP relaxes the muscle and increases blood flow.
Tadalafil blocks PDE5, the enzyme that breaks cGMP down. The label says it has no effect without sexual stimulation.
The same effect on cGMP is seen in the smooth muscle of the prostate, the bladder and their blood vessels. The label says how it reduces BPH symptoms has not been established.
Its half-life is 17.5 hours in healthy people, much longer than sildenafil's.
tadalafil alone, dissolved in the mouth.
tadalafil alone, chewed.

taken by mouth. The catalog does not say whether it is an FDA-approved generic or a compounded tablet.

what.text: The troches, gums, gummies, strips and dissolving tablets are compounded products. They are not FDA approved.

research.text: Tadalafil has a large body of randomized trials. The Cialis label says its use for ED was studied in 22 clinical trials of up to 24 weeks in more than 4,000 men. Four published studies are listed below as they were run, including one of tadalafil taken alongside sildenafil.

The label's main ED trials were 7 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies of 12 weeks, 2 in the US and 5 elsewhere. Food and alcohol were not restricted. The main measures were the erectile function part of the IIEF questionnaire and two questions from the Sexual Encounter Profile.

research.meta: Multinational · 2002 · Pooled analysis of 5 randomized trials
research.title: Erectile dysfunction, 5 trials pooled (J Urol 2002)

facts.v: Brock GB, McMahon CG, Chen KK, et al. J Urol 2002;168(4 Pt 1):1332-6
integrated analysis of 5 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials
1,112 men, mean age 59 (range 22 to 82), with mild to severe ED of various causes
tadalafil 2.5, 5, 10 or 20 mg or placebo, as needed, up to once daily, with no food or alcohol limits
12 weeks
IIEF erectile function score and Sexual Encounter Profile questions 2 and 3; a global question

research.found: On 20 mg, the IIEF erectile function score rose by a mean of 7.9 points from baseline (P<0.001 vs placebo). 75% of intercourse attempts were completed, and 81% reported better erections vs 35% on placebo. Headache and indigestion were the most frequent side effects.

src.label: Brock et al., J Urol, PubMed

research.title: Enlarged prostate (BPH) urinary symptoms (J Urol 2008)

facts.v: Roehrborn CG, McVary KT, Elion-Mboussa A, Viktrup L. J Urol 2008;180(4):1228-34
randomized, placebo-controlled, after a 4-week placebo run-in
1,058 men with urinary symptoms from BPH
tadalafil 2.5, 5, 10 or 20 mg or placebo, once daily
12 weeks
International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS); urine peak flow; IIEF erectile function

research.found: IPSS fell 3.9 to 5.2 points across tadalafil doses vs 2.3 on placebo (P=0.015 for 2.5 mg, P<0.001 for the others). Peak urine flow did not change significantly at any dose. Side effects were reported as infrequent.

src.label: Roehrborn et al., J Urol, PubMed

research.title: Pulmonary arterial hypertension, PHIRST (Circulation 2009)

facts.v: Galiè N, Brundage BH, Ghofrani HA, et al. Circulation 2009;119(22):2894-903
randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
405 people with PAH, either new to treatment or already taking bosentan
tadalafil 2.5, 10, 20 or 40 mg or placebo, once daily
16 weeks, with an optional long-term extension
change in 6-minute walk distance (main measure); WHO class, clinical worsening, quality of life

research.found: Walk distance rose with dose, but only the 40 mg dose met the preset level of significance (P<0.01); the overall placebo-corrected effect was 33 m. Changes in WHO class were not significant. Headache, muscle pain and flushing were the most common side effects.

research.title: Daily tadalafil with or without sildenafil as needed (Andrologia 2015)

facts.v: Cui H, Liu B, Song Z, et al. Andrologia 2015;47(1):20-4
two groups assigned 1:1. The abstract does not say whether the study was blinded or placebo-controlled.
180 men with ED
tadalafil 5 mg once daily alone, or tadalafil 5 mg once daily plus sildenafil 50 mg as needed
not stated in the abstract
IIEF-5 questionnaire, Sexual Encounter Profile, side effects

research.found: IIEF-5 scores were higher in the combined group among men with severe ED. Side-effect rates did not differ between groups. The two drugs were given on separate schedules; this was not a study of a single combined product.

research.text: A PubMed search for this page found no published human study of tadalafil given as a gum, gummy or troche, or combined with oxytocin or PT-141.

us.text: Tadalafil is FDA approved, by prescription, as Cialis (2003 for ED; 2011 for BPH, and for ED with BPH) and Adcirca (2009, PAH). The compounded forms Adonis carries through Beluga are not FDA approved. As of October 31, 2026.

items.text: approved November 21, 2003 (NDA 021368) as a new molecular entity, for erectile dysfunction.
on October 6, 2011, FDA approved two supplements: treatment of the signs and symptoms of BPH, and treatment of ED with the signs and symptoms of BPH.

src.label: FDA approval letter, NDA 021368/S-020 and S-021

items.text: approved May 22, 2009 (NDA 022332) for PAH (WHO Group 1), to improve exercise ability.

a chewable tadalafil tablet approved June 28, 2024 (NDA 218527) for ED, BPH, and ED with BPH. It is now listed as discontinued, and FDA determined it was not withdrawn for safety or effectiveness reasons. It is a different product from the compounded gums Adonis carries.
the label says tadalafil must not be used with any form of organic nitrate or with guanylate cyclase stimulators such as riociguat.

the Cialis label says combinations with other PDE5 inhibitors or ED treatments have not been studied, and tells prescribers to inform patients not to take Cialis with other PDE5 inhibitors, including Adcirca.
FDA's Drugs@FDA data list tadalafil combined only with finasteride or with macitentan. None combines it with sildenafil, oxytocin or PT-141.
taking tadalafil as a gum, gummy or troche, or in one dose with sildenafil, oxytocin or PT-141, is not an approved use. It is off-label.

us.text: The tadalafil troches, gums, gummies, strips and dissolving tablets Adonis carries through Beluga, including the combinations with sildenafil, oxytocin and PT-141, are compounded. Compounded drugs are not FDA approved.
FDA says compounded drugs are not FDA approved, which means FDA does not verify their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are marketed.

world.lead: Tadalafil is an approved prescription medicine in the US, the EU and Australia. In the UK, one 10 mg brand, Cialis Together, may be sold by pharmacists without a prescription. Canada's status is still being confirmed. It is not on WADA's Prohibited List.

countries.status: Approved medicine (Cialis 2003, ED; 2011, BPH and ED with BPH. Adcirca 2009, PAH). Prescription-only.
Status being confirmed with the regulator's record.

Cialis Together (tadalafil 10 mg) reclassified to pharmacy medicine in March 2023, for men over 18 with ED, at most one tablet a day and packs of up to 8. Other tadalafil medicines stay prescription-only.
Approved medicine. Cialis authorised November 12, 2002 (ED; also BPH); Adcirca authorised October 1, 2008 (PAH). Prescription-only.
Approved medicine: TGA publishes product information for Cialis, Adcirca and other tadalafil brands. Prescription-only (Schedule 4).

after.text: Canada: in January 2026, Health Canada warned about counterfeit Cialis and Viagra seized in Ontario. It described tadalafil and sildenafil as prescription drugs that should be used only under a health care professional's supervision and never with nitrate drugs.

after.text: Tadalafil is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or on the 2027 List, which takes effect January 1, 2027. It is not in the 2027 Monitoring Program either. Class S0 covers only substances with no government approval for human use, and tadalafil is approved (see above).

side.text: The label lists headache, indigestion and back pain as the most common side effects. Serious risks include a dangerous drop in blood pressure with nitrates, erections lasting more than 4 hours, sudden vision loss and sudden hearing loss.

items.text: in 8 placebo-controlled 12-week studies: headache (11% to 15% on tadalafil vs 5% on placebo), indigestion (4% to 10% vs 1%), back pain (3% to 6% vs 3%), muscle pain, stuffy nose, flushing and pain in a limb (up to 4%). 3.1% stopped for side effects on 10 or 20 mg, vs 1.4% on placebo.

contraindicated. If a man who has taken tadalafil needs a nitrate in a life-threatening emergency, the label says at least 48 hours should have passed since his last dose, with close medical monitoring.

ED treatments should not be used in men for whom sexual activity is inadvisable because of their heart condition. Men with recent heart attack, unstable angina, significant heart failure, uncontrolled arrhythmias, low or uncontrolled high blood pressure, or recent stroke were not included in the trials, and the label says Cialis is not recommended for them until more is known.
rare reports for this drug class. Priapism not treated promptly can permanently damage erectile tissue.

can be a sign of NAION, a type of optic nerve damage that can be permanent. Two observational studies cited in the label estimated about a 2-fold higher risk of NAION soon after PDE5 inhibitor use (2.15 and 2.27).
the label tells patients to stop and seek prompt care if hearing suddenly drops or is lost.
with alpha-blockers, blood-pressure medicines or substantial alcohol (5 units or more). CYP3A4 inhibitors such as ketoconazole and ritonavir raise tadalafil levels.
the Cialis label says combinations with other PDE5 inhibitors have not been studied, and patients should be told not to take them together. Several Adonis products combine tadalafil and sildenafil.
not recommended in pulmonary veno-occlusive disease; sudden vision or hearing loss can occur.

MHRA seized about 19.5 million doses of illegally traded ED medicines from 2021 to 2025, including tadalafil. It says such products may contain no active ingredient, the wrong dose, hidden drugs or toxic ingredients.

unconfirmed: Health Canada's Drug Product Database could not be reached, so no Canadian authorization of Cialis, Adcirca or another tadalafil brand is confirmed here.
TGA's ARTG (tga.gov.au) did not respond; Australian status rests on TGA's PI/CMI search and the Poisons Standard.
The Adonis catalog does not say whether its tadalafil 5 mg tablet is an FDA-approved generic or a compounded tablet.
The date FDA approved once-daily Cialis for ED was not confirmed from a Drugs@FDA record.
No published human study of tadalafil as a gum, gummy or troche, or with oxytocin or PT-141, was found; this rests on one PubMed search.
surprises: The Cialis label says to tell patients not to take it with other PDE5 inhibitors, yet several Adonis products put tadalafil and sildenafil in one dose.
FDA approved a chewable tadalafil tablet (Chewtadzy) in 2024, now discontinued; the tadalafil gums Adonis carries are compounded, not that approved product.
FDA's records list no approved product combining tadalafil with oxytocin or PT-141, although Adonis carries several such combinations.
